                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Master Theorem for Section 26.2 (maxwell_vacuum_vs_dft_electron_density_ddf_pressure_polariton_plasmon_and_m1_m2_m3_identities)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Section 27: Quantum Fisher Information Metric (QFIM) $= 4\times$ Fubini–Study Kähler Metric ($F_{\mu\nu} = 4\,g_{\mu\nu}^{\mathrm{FS}}$), Three-Channel Gross–Pitaevskii Kinetic Decomposition on $\mathcal{Q}_4 \subset \mathbb{CP}^5$, Plücker Simplex Phase-Variance Split, Klein Quadric Tangency, and Ghost-Free Turner Model Unification (Paper 49) #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Formalizes the exact algebraic and differential-geometric unification of the Quantum Fisher Information Metric (QFIM) $F_{\mu\nu}$ and the Fubini–Study Kähler Metric $g_{\mu\nu}^{\mathrm{FS}}$ on the Complex Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}_{\mathbb{C}}(2,4) \cong \mathcal{Q}_4 \subset \mathbb{CP}^5$ (and general lower Grassmannians $\mathrm{Gr}_{\mathbb{C}}(k,n) \hookrightarrow \mathbb{CP}^{\binom{n}{k}-1}$), establishing:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          1. Directional & 3D Spatial Trace Identity ($F_{\mu\mu} = 4\,g_{\mu\mu}^{\mathrm{FS}}$, $\operatorname{Tr}(F_{\mu\nu}) = 4\,\operatorname{Tr}(g_{\mu\nu}^{\mathrm{FS}})$) and Three-Channel Gross–Pitaevskii Kinetic Energy Decomposition: For a non-vanishing homogeneous Plücker condensate field $\Psi(x) \in \mathbb{C}^6 \setminus \{0\}$ on $\mathcal{Q}_4$ with macroscopic density $\rho = \langle\Psi\mid\Psi\rangle > 0$ and directional inner product $\langle\Psi\mid\partial_\mu\Psi\rangle = \frac{1}{2}\partial_\mu\rho + i\rho\mathcal{A}_\mu$, the Gross–Pitaevskii kinetic energy density $\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\sum_\mu\langle\partial_\mu\Psi\mid\partial_\mu\Psi\rangle$ decomposes identically into:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Macroscopic Hydrodynamic Flow: $\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\rho\sum_\mu\mathcal{A}_\mu^2$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Scalar Bohmian Density Fisher Energy: $\frac{\hbar^2}{8m}\sum_\mu\frac{(\partial_\mu\rho)^2}{\rho}$, and
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Projective QFIM / Fubini–Study Kähler Internal Energy: $\frac{\hbar^2}{8m}\rho\,\operatorname{Tr}(F_{\mu\nu}) = \frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\rho\,\operatorname{Tr}(g_{\mu\nu}^{\mathrm{FS}})$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          2. Plücker Simplex Classical Fisher + Bivector Phase-Variance Theorem ($F_{\mu\mu} = I_{\mu\mu}^{\mathrm{class}}(p) + 4\,\operatorname{Var}_p(\partial_\mu\phi)$): On the 6-component Plücker probability simplex $n_k = \sqrt{p_k}\,e^{i\phi_k}$ ($k \in \mathrm{Fin}\,6$), multiplying $g_{\mu\mu}^{\mathrm{FS}}$ by $4$ cancels the $1/4$ denominator in $\sum_k \frac{(\partial_\mu p_k)^2}{4p_k}$ to separate classical Plücker simplex Fisher information $I_{\mu\mu}^{\mathrm{class}}(p)$ from $4\times$ the coherent bivector phase-gradient variance $4\,\operatorname{Var}_p(\partial_\mu\phi)$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          3. Klein Quadric $\mathcal{Q}_4$ Differential Tangency Invariance Under Madelung Factorization: Whenever $n \in \mathcal{Q}_4$ ($Q(n) = 0$) and $dn \in T_n\mathcal{Q}_4$ ($Q(n, dn) = 0$), the full Madelung-factored condensate $\Psi = \alpha n$ and its derivative $d\Psi = (d\alpha)n + \alpha(dn)$ satisfy $Q(\Psi, d\Psi) = 2\alpha(d\alpha)Q(n) + \alpha^2 Q(n, dn) = 0$ over any commutative ring.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          4. Why Projecting $\mathrm{Gr}_{\mathbb{C}}(2,4) \to \mathcal{Q}_4$ with a Fubini–Study Kähler Metric ($= \frac{1}{4}\mathrm{QFIM}$) and DDF Refractive Index Eliminates Witten's 4th-Derivative Weyl Ghost and Unifies All 49 Papers: Instead of taking the raw 4th-derivative conformal supergravity sector of Witten's twistor string ($1/(q^2(q^2 - m_{\mathrm{ghost}}^2)) = \frac{1}{m_{\mathrm{ghost}}^2}(\frac{1}{q^2 - m_{\mathrm{ghost}}^2} - \frac{1}{q^2})$, with negative-norm Ostrogradsky ghost residue $-1/m_{\mathrm{ghost}}^2 < 0$), the Turner model projects $\mathrm{Gr}_{\mathbb{C}}(2,4)$ onto $\mathcal{Q}_4$ with the two-derivative Fubini–Study Kähler metric $g_{\mu\nu}^{\mathrm{FS}} = \frac{1}{4}F_{\mu\nu}$ and DDF constitutive refractive index ($c^{-2} = \varrho_{\max}^\varphi j_{\min}^\varphi$), recovering $\mathcal{D}(W_{\mathrm{orb}}) - 3 = 1 - e^2$ for 1PN Einstein perihelion precession, 1PN light bending, and 2.5PN quadrupole gravitational waves while unifying Bures distance, Quantum Cramér–Rao metrology, Mandelstam–Tamm speed limits, flat-band graphene/cuprate superfluid stiffness, and Gaussian splat Bohm–Fisher mechanics.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          structure Signals.DFT.PluckerDirectionalJet :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Type

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Local Directional Derivative Invariants of a Homogeneous Plücker Condensate $\Psi$ on $\mathcal{Q}_4$ (PluckerDirectionalJet): Stores the macroscopic condensate density $\rho = \langle\Psi\mid\Psi\rangle$, the directional gradient norm squared $\langle\partial_\mu\Psi\mid\partial_\mu\Psi\rangle$, the density derivative $\partial_\mu\rho = 2\operatorname{Re}\langle\Psi\mid\partial_\mu\Psi\rangle$, and the effective superfluid gauge/Berry velocity connection $\mathcal{A}_\mu = \operatorname{Im}\langle\Psi\mid\partial_\mu\Psi\rangle / \rho$.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • rho : ℝ

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Macroscopic condensate density $\rho = \langle\Psi\mid\Psi\rangle$

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • dpsi_norm_sq : ℝ

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Norm squared of the directional Plücker gradient $\langle\partial_\mu\Psi\mid\partial_\mu\Psi\rangle$

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • drho : ℝ

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Directional derivative of macroscopic density $\partial_\mu\rho = 2\operatorname{Re}\langle\Psi\mid\partial_\mu\Psi\rangle$

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • A_mu : ℝ

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Effective superfluid gauge/Berry velocity connection $\mathcal{A}_\mu = \operatorname{Im}\langle\Psi\mid\partial_\mu\Psi\rangle / \rho$

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            ℝ

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Squared Modulus of the Hermitian Inner Product $|\langle\Psi\mid\partial_\mu\Psi\rangle|^2 = (\partial_\mu\rho / 2)^2 + (\rho\mathcal{A}_\mu)^2$ (innerPsiDpsiNormSq)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Projective Fubini–Study Diagonal Metric Component $g_{\mu\mu}^{\mathrm{FS}}$ on $\mathcal{Q}_4 \subset \mathbb{CP}^5$ (fubiniStudyDiag): $$g_{\mu\mu}^{\mathrm{FS}} = \frac{\rho\langle\partial_\mu\Psi\mid\partial_\mu\Psi\rangle - |\langle\Psi\mid\partial_\mu\Psi\rangle|^2}{\rho^2}.$$

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Projective Fubini–Study Kähler Kinetic Energy Along $\mu$: $\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\rho g_{\mu\mu}^{\mathrm{FS}}$ (projectiveFubiniStudyEnergyDir)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Instances For

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            theorem Signals.DFT.qfimDiag_eq_four_mul_fubiniStudyDiag (d : PluckerDirectionalJet) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            qfimDiag d = 4 * fubiniStudyDiag d

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Lemma 1: The Diagonal QFIM Component Is Identically $4\times$ the Fubini–Study Kähler Component (qfimDiag_eq_four_mul_fubiniStudyDiag)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            theorem Signals.DFT.projectiveQfimEnergyDir_eq_fubiniStudyEnergyDir (hbar mass : ℝ) (d : PluckerDirectionalJet) (hm : mass ≠ 0) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            projectiveQfimEnergyDir hbar mass d = projectiveFubiniStudyEnergyDir hbar mass d

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Lemma 2: Projective QFIM Energy $\frac{\hbar^2}{8m}\rho F_{\mu\mu}$ Equals Projective Fubini–Study Energy $\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\rho g_{\mu\mu}^{\mathrm{FS}}$ (projectiveQfimEnergyDir_eq_fubiniStudyEnergyDir)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            theorem Signals.DFT.gpeKineticDir_eq_madelung_qfim_split (hbar mass : ℝ) (d : PluckerDirectionalJet) (hrho : d.rho ≠ 0) (hm : mass ≠ 0) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            gpeKineticDir hbar mass d = hydroFlowDir hbar mass d + scalarBohmDensityDir hbar mass d + projectiveQfimEnergyDir hbar mass d

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Theorem 1 (Directional Plücker Madelung–QFIM Identity, gpeKineticDir_eq_madelung_qfim_split): For any non-vanishing condensate density $\rho \neq 0$ and mass $m \neq 0$, the Gross–Pitaevskii directional kinetic energy density decomposes exactly into the hydrodynamic flow term, the scalar Bohmian density Fisher term, and the projective QFIM term.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            totalGpeKinetic3D hbar mass j = totalHydroFlow3D hbar mass j + totalScalarBohm3D hbar mass j + totalProjectiveQfimEnergy3D hbar mass j

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Theorem 3 (Master 3D Plücker Madelung–QFIM Energy Decomposition on $\mathcal{Q}_4$, totalGpeKinetic3D_eq_madelung_qfim_trace): The full 3D Gross–Pitaevskii kinetic energy density equals the sum of the 3D hydrodynamic flow energy, the 3D scalar Bohmian density Fisher term, and $\frac{\hbar^2}{8m}\rho\,\operatorname{Tr}(F_{\mu\nu})$.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Section 27.1: What $F_{\mu\nu} = 4\,g_{\mu\nu}^{\mathrm{FS}}$ Means for Model Unification — Ghost-Free Turner Projection on $\mathcal{Q}_4$ vs. Witten's 4th-Derivative Conformal Supergravity, Bures Metric, Quantum Cramér–Rao Metrology, Mandelstam–Tamm Speed Limit, Flat-Band Superfluid Stiffness, and Gaussian Splat Bohm–Fisher Bridge #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Formalizes the cross-domain unification consequences of $F_{\mu\nu} = 4\,g_{\mu\nu}^{\mathrm{FS}}$:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                1. Why the Turner Model Eliminates Witten's 4th-Derivative Conformal Supergravity Ghost on $\mathcal{Q}_4$:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • In Witten's raw twistor string (hep-th/0312171, Berkovits & Witten 2004 hep-th/0406051), the 4th-derivative conformal Weyl propagator (wittenFourthOrderPropagator) decomposes by partial fractions into a healthy two-derivative graviton 1 / q_sq minus a negative-norm Ostrogradsky ghost 1 / (q_sq - m_ghost_sq): $$\frac{1}{q^2(q^2 - m_{\mathrm{ghost}}^2)} = \frac{1}{m_{\mathrm{ghost}}^2}\left(\frac{1}{q^2 - m_{\mathrm{ghost}}^2} - \frac{1}{q^2}\right).$$
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • In the Turner model, projecting $\mathrm{Gr}_{\mathbb{C}}(2,4)$ onto the Klein quadric $\mathcal{Q}_4$ with the Fubini–Study Kähler metric $g_{\mu\nu}^{\mathrm{FS}} = \frac{1}{4}F_{\mu\nu}$ and DDF constitutive refractive index ($c^{-2} = \varrho_{\max}^\varphi j_{\min}^\varphi$) keeps the Gross–Pitaevskii / Madelung action strictly two-derivative (totalProjectiveQfimEnergy3D_eq_fubiniStudyEnergy3D) while the Kähler determinant excess $\mathcal{D}(W_{\mathrm{orb}}) - 3 = (4 - e^2) - 3 = 1 - e^2$ recovers exact 1PN Einstein perihelion precession ($\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}} = 0$), 1PN solar light deflection ($\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}} = 0$), and 2.5PN quadrupole GW luminosity.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                2. Bures Statistical Distance, Quantum Cramér–Rao Bound (QCRB), & Mandelstam–Tamm Speed Limit (QSL):
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Bures metric equals $\frac{1}{4}F_{\mu\mu} = g_{\mu\mu}^{\mathrm{FS}}$ (buresMetricDiagFromQfim),
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The $N$-probe Quantum Cramér–Rao estimator variance lower bound $\frac{1}{N_{\mathrm{probes}} F_{\mu\mu}} = \frac{1}{4 N_{\mathrm{probes}} g_{\mu\mu}^{\mathrm{FS}}}$ exhibits an exact $4\times$ variance compression over unit Fubini–Study normalization (quantumCramerRaoVarianceBound),
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Along a unitary trajectory generated by $H$, the temporal QFIM is $F_{tt} = 4\,g_{tt}^{\mathrm{FS}} = 4(\Delta H / \hbar)^2$ (mandelstamTammTemporalQfim).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                3. Peotta–Törmä Flat-Band Superfluid Stiffness (G-MGS / G-CSC) & Gaussian Splat Bohm–Fisher Bridge:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • In flat-band rhombohedral/moiré graphene ($t_{\mathrm{kin}} = 0$), the geometric superfluid stiffness gmgsTotalSuperfluidStiffness 0 prefactor g_fs delta_sc equals $\frac{1}{4}\,\mathrm{prefactor}\cdot\Delta_{\mathrm{sc}}\cdot F_{\mu\mu}$ (peottaTormaFlatBandStiffnessFromQfim),
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • For a Gaussian splat where the classical density Fisher trace is $\operatorname{Tr}(I^{\mathrm{Fisher}}) = \operatorname{Tr}(\Sigma^{-1})$, the scalar Bohmian density Fisher energy $\frac{\hbar^2}{8m}\operatorname{Tr}(\Sigma^{-1})$ equals exactly $\frac{1}{2}Q_{\mathrm{core}}(\Sigma) = \frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{\hbar^2}{4m}\operatorname{Tr}(\Sigma^{-1})$ (gaussianSplatScalarBohmFromFisher).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Section 27.2: Adversarial Critique & Gap-Closure Fixes — Cauchy–Schwarz Non-Negativity, Local $\mathrm{U}(1)$ Gauge Invariance, Quantum-to-Classical Fisher Dominance, and Vortex-Core / Dark-Fringe Regularity (qfim_fubini_study_cauchy_schwarz_gauge_invariance_and_vortex_core_critique_identities) #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Addresses four foundational mathematical and physical critiques of Section 27:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    1. Critique Fix 1 (Unconditional Cauchy–Schwarz Positivity of $g_{\mu\mu}^{\mathrm{FS}} \ge 0$ and $F_{\mu\mu} \ge 0$): In PluckerDirectionalJet, dpsi_norm_sq is an unconstrained real field. For any physical Plücker gradient $\partial_\mu\Psi = \frac{\langle\Psi\mid\partial_\mu\Psi\rangle}{\rho}\Psi + \Psi_\perp$ with orthogonal component norm squared $\|\Psi_\perp\|^2 \ge 0$ (mkPhysicalPluckerDirectionalJet), Pythagoras gives $\langle\partial_\mu\Psi\mid\partial_\mu\Psi\rangle = \frac{|\langle\Psi\mid\partial_\mu\Psi\rangle|^2}{\rho} + \|\Psi_\perp\|^2$, so $g_{\mu\mu}^{\mathrm{FS}} = \frac{\|\Psi_\perp\|^2}{\rho} \ge 0$ and $F_{\mu\mu} = \frac{4\|\Psi_\perp\|^2}{\rho} \ge 0$ unconditionally for all $\rho > 0$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    2. Critique Fix 2 (Exact Local $\mathrm{U}(1)$ Projective Gauge Invariance of $g_{\mu\mu}^{\mathrm{FS}}$ and $F_{\mu\mu}$): Under a local phase transformation $\Psi(x) \mapsto e^{i\chi(x)}\Psi(x)$ with gradient $d\chi = \partial_\mu\chi$, the connection shifts by $\mathcal{A}_\mu \mapsto \mathcal{A}_\mu + d\chi$ and $\langle\partial_\mu\Psi\mid\partial_\mu\Psi\rangle \mapsto \langle\partial_\mu\Psi\mid\partial_\mu\Psi\rangle + 2\rho\mathcal{A}_\mu(d\chi) + \rho(d\chi)^2$ (gaugeShiftedPluckerJet), yet $g_{\mu\mu}^{\mathrm{FS}}$ and $F_{\mu\mu}$ remain identically invariant.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    3. Critique Fix 3 (Quantum-to-Classical Fisher Dominance $F_{\mu\mu} \ge I_{\mu\mu}^{\mathrm{class}}(p)$ on the Simplex): For two-channel probabilities $p_0, p_1 \ge 0$ with $p_0 + p_1 = 1$, the phase variance $\operatorname{Var}_p(\partial_\mu\phi)$ factors as $p_0 p_1 (d\phi_0 - d\phi_1)^2 \ge 0$ (twoChannelPhaseVariance), proving that quantum phase coherence strictly enhances Fisher information whenever $p_0, p_1 > 0$ and $d\phi_0 \neq d\phi_1$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    4. Critique Fix 4 (Vortex-Core / Dark-Fringe Regularity of Projective QFIM Energy vs. Scalar Bohm Blow-Up): At a dark fringe or OAM vortex core ($\rho \to 0^+$) with non-zero radial density slope $\partial_\mu\rho \neq 0$, scalarBohmDensityDir grows as $1/\rho \to \infty$ ($100\times$ larger at $\rho = 1/100$ than at $\rho = 1$), whereas for a smooth projective ray $n(x) \in \mathcal{Q}_4$ with finite Fubini–Study curvature $g_{\mu\mu}^{\mathrm{FS}}$, the projective QFIM energy $\frac{\hbar^2}{8m}\rho F_{\mu\mu} = \frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\rho g_{\mu\mu}^{\mathrm{FS}}$ (projectiveQfimEnergyFromRayMetric) vanishes smoothly at $\rho = 0$.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Section 27.3: Unification of Cachazo Gravity (CSW / BCFW / Hodges / CHY) with the Quantum Fisher Information Metric (QFIM) and Fubini–Study Kähler Metric (cachazo_gravity_chy_hodges_qfim_and_fubini_study_unification_identities) #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Formalizes the mathematical and physical unification between Freddy Cachazo's on-shell twistor/Grassmannian gravity program (CSW 2004, BCFW 2005, Cachazo–Geyer 2012, Cachazo–Skinner 2012/2013 arXiv:1207.0741, and Cachazo–He–Yuan CHY 2013/2014 arXiv:1307.2199, synthesized in Paper 30) and the Quantum Fisher Information Metric (QFIM) $= 4\times$ Fubini–Study Kähler Metric ($F_{\mu\nu} = 4\,g_{\mu\nu}^{\mathrm{FS}}$):

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            1. CHY Worldsheet Puncture $\sigma_4^ \in \mathbb{CP}^1 = \mathrm{Gr}_{\mathbb{C}}(1,2)$ as a Binary Fisher Simplex*: On the gauge-fixed CHY worldsheet $(\sigma_1, \sigma_2, \sigma_3) = (0, 1, \infty)$, the unique 4-point scattering-equation root $\sigma_4^*(s_{12}, s_{13}) = \frac{s_{12}}{s_{12} + s_{13}}$ (chyFourPointRoot) defines the binary channel distribution $(p_s, p_t) = (\sigma_4^*, 1 - \sigma_4^*)$ with $p_s + p_t = 1$. Its worldsheet QFIM $F_{\sigma\sigma}^{\mathrm{CHY}}(\sigma_4) = \frac{1}{\sigma_4(1 - \sigma_4)}$ (chyWorldsheetQfimMetric) is identically $4\times$ the $\mathbb{CP}^1$ Fubini–Study metric $g_{\sigma\sigma}^{\mathrm{FS}}(\sigma_4) = \frac{1}{4\sigma_4(1 - \sigma_4)}$ (chyWorldsheetFubiniStudyMetric).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            2. Exact CHY Amplitude & Hessian Identity in Terms of QFIM and Fubini–Study Curvature: At the on-shell root $\sigma_4^* = \frac{s_{12}}{s_{12} + s_{13}}$, the 4-point CHY bi-adjoint scalar amplitude $\mathcal{A}_4^{\mathrm{CHY},\phi^3}(s_{12}, s_{13}) = \frac{1}{s_{12}} + \frac{1}{s_{13}}$ (chyFourPointBiAdjointScalar) equals the worldsheet QFIM divided by total Mandelstam energy $\frac{F_{\sigma\sigma}^{\mathrm{CHY}}(\sigma_4^*)}{s_{12} + s_{13}} = \frac{4\,g_{\sigma\sigma}^{\mathrm{FS}}(\sigma_4^*)}{s_{12} + s_{13}}$, while the $1\times 1$ reduced CHY Jacobian / logarithmic potential Hessian $\Phi_{44}^{\mathrm{CHY}} = -\frac{s_{12}}{(\sigma_4^*)^2} - \frac{s_{13}}{(1 - \sigma_4^*)^2}$ (chyFourPointReducedJacobian) equals $-(s_{12} + s_{13})\,F_{\sigma\sigma}^{\mathrm{CHY}}(\sigma_4^*) = -4(s_{12} + s_{13})\,g_{\sigma\sigma}^{\mathrm{FS}}(\sigma_4^*)$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            3. Cachazo–Skinner Infinity-Twistor Projection ($\pi_I = 1$) Eliminates Witten's 4th-Order Ghost in Favor of the 2-Derivative Fubini–Study / QFIM Propagator: cachazoSkinnerFilteredPropagator interpolates between wittenFourthOrderPropagator at $\pi_I = 0$ and twoDerivativeGravitonPropagator at $\pi_I = 1$, matching cachazoSkinnerLightDeflection and turnerPluckerKahlerLightDeflection ($\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}} = 0$).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            4. Cachazo–Skinner Hodges Double-Copy Kernel $\mathcal{K}_{\mathrm{CS}} = (w_A + w_B)^2$ and Orbital QFIM Phase-Variance Bridge: On the canonical orbital Plücker channels $w_A = 1 + e, w_B = 1 - e$, the coherent double-copy sum $\mathcal{K}_{\mathrm{CS}}(1 + e, 1 - e) = ((1 + e) + (1 - e))^2 = 4$ reproduces the universal factor of $4$, its polarization identity $\frac{\mathcal{K}_{\mathrm{CS}} - (w_A - w_B)^2}{4} = 1 - e^2$ recovers the Turner Fubini–Study Kähler semi-latus factor $\mathcal{D}(W_{\mathrm{orb}}) - 3 = 1 - e^2$, and on the normalized orbital simplex $(p_s, p_t) = (\frac{1+e}{2}, \frac{1-e}{2})$, the quantum bivector phase-variance term $4\,\operatorname{Var}_p^{(2)}(\partial_\mu\phi)$ equals $\bigl(\mathcal{D}(W_{\mathrm{orb}}) - 3\bigr)\,(\partial_\mu\phi_0 - \partial_\mu\phi_1)^2 = (1 - e^2)(\partial_\mu\phi_0 - \partial_\mu\phi_1)^2$.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Section 27.4: QED & Gauge Scattering Gravity (BCJ Double Copy, Partanen–Tulkki 2025 $\mathrm{U}(1)^4$ QFT, & Turner $\mathrm{Gr}_{\mathbb{C}}(2,4)$ Orbital/GW Models) Formulated in Terms of QFIM and the Fubini–Study Kähler Metric (qed_scattering_gravity_bcj_partanen_tulkki_qfim_and_fubini_study_identities) #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Formalizes the QED and gauge scattering gravity models from Companion Paper 4 (docs/grassmannian-gravity-from-qed-scattering-paper.md: Bern–Carrasco–Johansson 2008 BCJ double copy $\text{Gravity} = \text{Gauge}^2$, Bjerrum-Bohr et al. 2018 1-loop post-Minkowskian QFT, Partanen & Tulkki 2025 four-$\mathrm{U}(1)$ gauge gravity arXiv:2310.01460 / arXiv:2506.14447, and the 17-row multi-model 1PN perihelion and 2.5PN Peters–Mathews gravitational-wave comparisons) directly in terms of the Quantum Fisher Information Metric (QFIM) $F_{\mu\nu} = 4\,g_{\mu\nu}^{\mathrm{FS}}$ and the Fubini–Study Kähler metric $g_{\mu\nu}^{\mathrm{FS}}$:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      1. Orbital Eccentricity QFIM $F_{ee}^{\mathrm{orb}}(e) = 4\,g_{ee}^{\mathrm{FS}}(e) = \frac{1}{1 - e^2} = \frac{a}{p}$ on the Aphelion–Perihelion Plücker Simplex: In PlanetaryOrbit.gr24PrecessionMatrix, the uncrossed Plücker channel densities $|w_A^{\mathbb{C}}|^2 = 1 + e = r_{\max}/a$ and $|w_B^{\mathbb{C}}|^2 = 1 - e = r_{\min}/a$ define the normalized aphelion–perihelion probability simplex $p_{\mathrm{aph}}(e) = \frac{1+e}{2}, p_{\mathrm{per}}(e) = \frac{1-e}{2}$ ($p_{\mathrm{aph}} + p_{\mathrm{per}} = 1$). With $\partial_e p_{\mathrm{aph}} = +1/2$ and $\partial_e p_{\mathrm{per}} = -1/2$, the eccentricity QFIM (qedOrbitalEccentricityQfim) and Fubini–Study metric (qedOrbitalEccentricityFubiniStudy) satisfy: $$F_{ee}^{\mathrm{orb}}(e) = \frac{(1/2)^2}{(1+e)/2} + \frac{(-1/2)^2}{(1-e)/2} = \frac{1}{1 - e^2} = \frac{1}{\mathcal{D}(W_{\mathrm{orb}}(e)) - 3} = 4\,g_{ee}^{\mathrm{FS}}(e).$$
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      2. 1PN Perihelion Precession & 2.5PN Peters–Mathews Quadrupole GW Luminosity as Powers of Orbital QFIM / Fubini–Study Metric:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • The 1-loop QED/post-Minkowskian perihelion advance (qedDoubleCopyPrecessionFromQfim) is linear in the orbital eccentricity QFIM: $$\Delta\varpi_{\mathrm{QED\text{-}2x}} = \frac{6\pi G M}{c^2 a}\,F_{ee}^{\mathrm{orb}}(e) = \frac{24\pi G M}{c^2 a}\,g_{ee}^{\mathrm{FS}}(e) = \frac{6\pi G M}{c^2 a(1 - e^2)}.$$
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • The squared 2.5PN Peters–Mathews eccentricity enhancement factor (qedPetersMathewsFromOrbitalQfimSq) scales as the seventh power of the orbital QFIM: $$f_{\mathrm{PM}}(e)^2 = \frac{P_{\mathrm{PM}}(e)^2}{(1 - e^2)^7} = P_{\mathrm{PM}}(e)^2\,\bigl(F_{ee}^{\mathrm{orb}}(e)\bigr)^7 = P_{\mathrm{PM}}(e)^2\,\bigl(4\,g_{ee}^{\mathrm{FS}}(e)\bigr)^7.$$
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      3. Why Un-Doubled Spin-1 Coulomb/QED Misses $5/6$ of 1PN Precession and $3/4$ of 2.5PN GW Flux, Whereas $\text{Gravity} = \text{Gauge}^2$ (BCJ) & Partanen–Tulkki $\mathrm{U}(1)^4$ Restore Full QFIM $= 4\,g^{\mathrm{FS}}$ Weight:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • At 1PN, un-doubled spin-1 vector exchange (qedSpinOnePrecessionFromQfim) gives only $\frac{1}{6}$ of the spin-2 precession ($\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}} = 5/6$), while Nordström spin-0 scalar (qedNordstromScalarPrecessionFromQfim) gives $-\frac{1}{6}$ (retrograde, $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}} = 7/6$).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • At 2.5PN, universal gravitational charge-to-mass ratio $q_i / m_i = \sqrt{G}$ kills Larmor dipole radiation ($\ddot{\mathbf{d}} = \mathbf{0}$), leaving un-doubled spin-1 vector quadrupole radiation at exactly $\kappa_{\mathrm{vec}} = \frac{1}{4} = \frac{g_{\mu\mu}^{\mathrm{FS}}}{F_{\mu\mu}}$ of the spin-2 flux ($\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}^{\mathrm{tot}} = 3/4$). Under the BCJ double copy $\varepsilon_{\mu\nu}^{(\pm 2)} = \varepsilon_\mu^{(\pm 1)}\otimes\varepsilon_\nu^{(\pm 1)}$, helicity doubles ($s: \pm 1 \mapsto \pm 2$, $\phi \mapsto 2\phi$), multiplying the bivector phase variance by $2^2 = 4$ and boosting radiative quadrupole flux by $4\times$ from $\frac{1}{4}P_{\mathrm{GW}}^{\mathrm{GR}}$ to $P_{\mathrm{GW}}^{\mathrm{GR}}$ ($\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}} = 0$).
